title: Free integral modules on constant residue groups are the actual residue diagram
statement: Let X be a scheme and l a prime. Set R_X=p_X^*continuousMapRingObj(Z_l). Let C_n be the constant abelian sheaf on ULift(ZMod(l^n)), with transitions induced by the usual reduction homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let Q_n be the actual R_X-module of continuous ZMod(l^n)-valued functions, with action through chartComparison followed by PadicInt.toZModPow and the actual reduction transitions of [lem-poincare-integral-residue-module-limit]. Then the diagrams n|->Mod.freeFunctor(R_X)(C_n) [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists] and n|->Q_n are naturally isomorphic. Both include n=0. No invertibility or finiteness assumption on X is required.

source.place: The actual integral coefficient quotient and free-module comparison, compatible with all residue reductions.

proof.text: For every site object U, reduction C(U,Z_l)->C(U,Z/l^n) is surjective: compose a residue-valued function with its integer representatives. A continuous integral function with zero residue divides continuously by l^n: divide in Q_l, use the residue norm bound to land in Z_l, and use continuity of division by a fixed nonzero scalar. Thus the reduction is the cokernel of multiplication by l^n, sectionwise and hence in abelian sheaves.

Transfer this cokernel across the canonical chartComparison from the actual integral coefficient object, and reflect the underlying colimit through the module forgetful functor. Independently, Z/l^n is the cokernel of multiplication by l^n on the integral tensor unit in Ab: its integer projection is surjective with kernel nZ. Constant sheafification and the free internal-module functor preserve that cokernel. Their monoidal unit comparison identifies its source with the regular integral coefficient module.

Uniqueness of cokernels gives an explicit linear level isomorphism from the free module on the constant residue group to the actual residue module of [lem-poincare-integral-residue-module-limit]. The defining projection identity of this comparison makes the transition squares commute: precompose with the epic integer projection and use castHom compatibility. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the level maps, all of which are isomorphisms. The argument includes n=0 and empty schemes.

    Nonempty (constantTateResidueSystem X ℓ ⋙
      Mod.freeFunctor (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ]) X) ≅
        tateResidueModuleSystem X ℓ)
